headline: Hike fears cool AI megacaps as holiday session looks to stabilize
body: The dominant story this week has been a sharp repricing of Fed policy: hotter-than-expected core PCE inflation (3.3% versus a 3.2% forecast) pushed the probability of a December rate hike toward the mid-90s percent, a stark reversal from the rate-cutting path markets had assumed through most of 2026. That shift has hit the most richly valued corners of the market hardest — Nvidia has fallen as much as 30% from its October record near $243, and the Nasdaq 100 briefly traded roughly 20% below its own peak, correction territory for the index's AI-linked leadership. The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq clawed back some of those losses into Wednesday's close ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, and futures were pointing higher again heading into today's shortened Black Friday session, suggesting dip-buyers are testing the selloff rather than extending it.

Sentiment readings have leaned more defensive than the price action alone suggests: several recent surveys of individual investors show bullish responses sliding and bearish ones climbing, consistent with a market that spent weeks pricing in rate cuts and is now adjusting to the opposite. Retail chatter on Reddit and StockTwits has centered on the same handful of AI bellwethers, but there's little concrete, same-day social signal to point to given the holiday-shortened week — this read leans more on index-level price action and the Fed/inflation narrative than on social-media positioning. With trading volume typically thin on the post-Thanksgiving half-day, today's session looks less like a verdict on the selloff and more like a low-conviction gauge of whether Wednesday's bounce has legs once full liquidity returns next week.
